```{r setup}
library(chromatographR)
```

##### 1. How should I format my data for analysis in `chromatographR`?

`chromatographR` functions expect chromatograms to be in wide format with retention times as rownames. Thus, if you have a csv file with retention times in the first column, you should be able to read the files into R as follows:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
lapply(vector_of_file_paths, function(f){
  read.csv(f, row.names = 1)
})
```

If you have chromatograms in "long" format, you will need to reshape them into wide format before proceeding with the analysis.

\n

##### 2. Some of my peaks aren't being integrated when I run `get_peaks`.

Try adjusting the value of the `max_fwhm` argument, especially if you are seeing that your wider peaks are the ones that aren't being integrated. This argument sets the maximum peak width (as a full width at half maximum) that will be kept; what's "sensible" varies with the resolution of your data, so the default (`max_fwhm = 0.5`) won't fit every dataset. For example, in the example shown below, wider peaks will not be picked up with `max_fwhm = 0.12`, but if we increase `max_fwhm` to `0.5`, we are able to successfully integrate all of our peaks. If this fails, try adjusting the `smooth_window`.

```{r}
data(Sa_pr)
par(mfrow=c(2,1))
pks <- get_peaks(Sa_warp, lambdas = "210", fit = "egh", max_fwhm = 0.12)
plot(pks, main = "`max_fwhm` = 0.12")

pks <- get_peaks(Sa_warp, lambdas = "210", fit = "egh", max_fwhm = 0.5)
plot(pks, main = "`max_fwhm` = 0.5")
```
